items.name: Omega x Swatch
clues: A watch that people queued round the block for, in several countries at once.
It came out in March 2022, in eleven versions named after the Sun, the Moon and the planets.
People who could never afford a luxury watch, and collectors who already own one.
It copies the shape of a famous watch worn on the Moon, but it’s made of a ceramic-and-plastic mix and costs about 250 euros.
Both brands belong to the same Swiss group. One is a luxury watchmaker; the other makes cheap, colourful plastic watches.
The MoonSwatch.

items.name: Ray-Ban x Meta
clues: Sunglasses that can listen to you, film for you and talk back.
The first pair came out in September 2021, a few weeks before one of the partners changed its company name.
People who want to film their bike ride or a concert without holding up a phone.
They look like ordinary classic sunglasses, apart from two tiny cameras and a little light that shows people nearby when they are recording.
One partner is a sunglasses brand first made for American pilots in the 1930s; the other owns Facebook and Instagram.
Smart glasses from Mark Zuckerberg's company, in the brand famous for Aviators and Wayfarers.

items.name: Puma x Rihanna
clues: A pop star became creative director of a sportswear brand, instead of just appearing in its adverts.
She took the job in December 2014, and her first shoe came out the following autumn.
Young fans of her music who were far more interested in fashion than in sport.
Her first shoe had a thick, ridged sole and was called the Creeper. The first batch sold out in three hours.
In 2016 the Creeper was named Shoe of the Year by Footwear News.
The German sportswear brand with the leaping cat and the singer of “Umbrella”, under the name Fenty.

items.name: IKEA x Sonos
clues: Furniture that plays music.
The first products came out in 2019.
People who want good sound at home but don’t want ugly black boxes everywhere.
A speaker that is also a bookshelf, a speaker that is also a table lamp, and later one that hangs on the wall like a picture.
A Swedish furniture giant and an American wireless speaker company. The range has a Swedish name meaning “symphonic”.
Flat-pack furniture meets wireless speakers: the SYMFONISK range.

items.name: Absolut x Andy Warhol
clues: A drinks bottle turned into a work of art.
It happened in New York in the mid-1980s.
People at parties who like to think they have good taste.
The artist painted the brand’s bottle, the painting became an advert, and it started a long series with other artists.
The drink is from Sweden. The artist is famous for soup cans and portraits of Marilyn Monroe.
A Swedish vodka and the king of pop art.

items.name: Milka x Oreo
clues: Two snacks your little brother or sister would fight you for, in one.
Both brands belong to the same big American snack company.
Anyone in a supermarket queue who can’t decide between biscuits and chocolate.
A lilac wrapper with a black-and-white biscuit on it.
One is a chocolate brand from the Alps with a lilac cow. The other is an American sandwich biscuit first sold in 1912.
Lilac-cow chocolate with pieces of the world’s best-known black-and-white cream biscuit inside.
